# ComposedSurface

Draws Ouro's composed tree with Ouro HX, whatever format it came in: core's `ComposedNode`, from A2UI messages, an MCP tool result's `structuredContent.ouro`, or your own code. Every button is one of your app's declared actions: read and write run, a consequential one asks the person to confirm what the agent prepared, and a person-only one takes them to your app's own screen. Its fields (TextField, Checkbox, Select) fill in `data`, and a button bound to a field sends what the person entered.

```tsx
import { ComposedSurface } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/composed-surface/composed-surface";
```

## Example

```tsx
<ComposedSurface
  tree={result.structuredContent.ouro.tree}
  data={result.structuredContent.ouro.data}
  onPress={(press) => callTool(press.action, press.input)}
  onHandoff={({ action }) => navigate(`/recipes/${id}?do=${action}`)}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use A2UISurface instead for A2UI messages, and HX's components directly when your own code, not an agent, decides the layout.

## Props

Type: `ComposedSurfaceProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width (`max-w-md`). |
| `components` | `Readonly<Record<string, ComposedRenderer>>` | {} | Your app's own components, by the name your catalog declares them under (the actions file's `components` export): a renderer draws its component and may use HX's components. A name left out of the map is left out of the drawing, and a development message names the fix. |
| `data` | `Obj` | {} | The data model the tree's fields start from, such as an MCP tool result's `structuredContent.ouro.data`. A TextField, Checkbox or Select shows what it holds at the field's `value` pointer and writes the person's answer there. A button input bound to that pointer (`{"@path": "/servings"}`) sends the answer when the person presses, and a consequential button's confirm sheet shows it. When `data` or `tree` changes, as an agent's update changes them, what the person entered stays, except at a pointer whose value the new `data` changed, or in a list item it changed: there the agent's value wins. |
| `onHandoff` (required) | `(handoff: ComposedHandoff) => void` |  | A person-only button never runs from composed UI: take the person to your app's own screen for it. |
| `onPress` (required) | `(press: PersonPress, button: ComposedNode) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Runs a pressed read or write button, and a consequential one once the person confirms. `press` is core's `PersonPress` (the action, the prepared input, its consent, and that the person pressed it); `button` is the node, for a format that names its source. Return a promise to show the button loading until it settles. |
| `tree` (required) | `ComposedNode` |  | The composed tree to draw: core's `ComposedNode`, its values resolved. Check one you didn't resolve yourself with core's `validateTree` against the app's catalog first; A2UI's resolver already has. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `dataModel`: Not a prop. The fields' data model is `data`: `<ComposedSurface data={structuredContent.ouro.data}>`.
- `onAction`: Not a prop. A pressed button calls `onPress`, or `onHandoff` for a person-only one: `<ComposedSurface onPress={run} onHandoff={openApp}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `ComposedHandoff`

Where a person-only button takes the person: the action's id and the catalog's `how`.

```ts
interface ComposedHandoff {
  action: string;
  how: string;
}
```

### `ComposedRenderer`

Draws one of your app's own components, the ones your catalog declares beyond Ouro HX's: `node.props` holds its resolved props (core's `asText` text, booleans, lists) and `children` its children, already drawn.

```ts
type ComposedRenderer = (node: ComposedNode, children: ReactNode[]) => ReactNode;
```
